


Typical graphs for the beta PDF are given in Fig.\ \@ref(fig:BetaDistributions). 
When $m = n$, the distribution is symmetric about $x = \frac{1}{2}$.



```{r BetaDistributions, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center", fig.cap="Various beta-distribution PDFs.", fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5, out.width='80%'}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

x <- seq(0, 1, 
         length = 100)

m <- c(0.5, 0.1, 4, 6)
n <- c(0.5, 2, 4, 2)


plot( x = x,
      y = dbeta(x = x,
                shape1 = m[1],
                shape2 = n[1]),
      xlab = expression(italic(x)),
      ylab = "Probability function",
      lwd = 2,
      type = "l",
      las = 1,
      ylim = c(0, 3),
      main = "Beta distributions")
lines( x = x,
       y = dbeta(x = x,
                 shape1 = m[2],
                 shape2 = n[2]),
       lwd = 2,
       lty = 2)
lines( x = x,
       y = dbeta(x = x,
                 shape1 = m[3],
                 shape2 = n[3]),
       lwd = 2,
       lty = 3)
lines( x = x,
       y = dbeta(x = x,
                 shape1 = m[4],
                 shape2 = n[4]),
       lwd = 2,
       lty = 4)

# Now have a panel just for the legend!
plot( x = c(1, 5),
      y = c(1, 5),
      axes = FALSE,
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      type = "n")

legend("right",
       lty = 1:4,
       lwd = 2,
       bty = "n",
       legend = c( bquote(italic(m)== .(m[1])~and~italic(n)==.(n[1])),
                   bquote(italic(m)== .(m[2])~and~italic(n)==.(n[2])),
                   bquote(italic(m)== .(m[3])~and~italic(n)==.(n[3])),
                   bquote(italic(m)== .(m[4])~and~italic(n)==.(n[4])) )
)



```
